blocks.heading: The first 5 minutes
lines: Give each set about 40 seconds before you commit to any.
Read the setup and the first two questions. Do not start solving.
Mark each set: do now, maybe later, or skip.
By minute 5, pick two sets and start the easier one.

blocks.heading: Signs a set is doable
lines: A fixed number of people, seats or slots, with clear conditions.
Questions that each ask for one fact from the finished grid.
Data that fits one table without guessing its shape.
Friendly numbers: round totals and small counts.

blocks.heading: Signs to skip or leave for later
lines: Long text full of 'at least', 'at most' and 'either or' conditions.
Every question adds a new condition, so one grid answers none of them.
Heavy arithmetic on awkward numbers with options close together.
After two readings you still cannot see where to start.

blocks.heading: Picking 2 sets of 4
lines: Two sets solved fully usually score more than four sets half done.
Prefer the set whose grid you can start within a minute, even if it looks longer.
If a set has no grid after 4 minutes, move to your third choice.
Type-in questions carry no negative mark, so enter an answer for each one in a set you have worked on.
